### pre processing

```{r}
# Load dataset
data <- fread("data/brca_metabric_clinical_data.tsv")
```

```{r}
# Check if Sample ID and Patient ID are identical
identical_ids <- identical(data$`Sample ID`, data$`Patient ID`)
cat("Are 'Sample ID' and 'Patient ID' identical? →", identical_ids, "\n")

# Check unique values in cancer type, Study ID, Sample Type, Number of Samples Per Patient
unique_cancer_types <- unique(data$`Cancer Type`)
unique_study_ids <- unique(data$`Study ID`)
unique_sample_types <- unique(data$`Sample Type`)
unique_numbers_of_samples_per_patient<-unique(data$`Number of Samples Per Patient`)

#cat("Unique values in 'Cancer Type':", length(unique_cancer_types), "\n")
#cat("Unique values in 'Study ID':", length(unique_study_ids), "\n")
cat("Unique values in 'Study ID','Cancer Type','Sample Type','Number of Samples Per Patient' : ", length(unique_cancer_types), length(unique_study_ids), length(unique_sample_types), length(unique_numbers_of_samples_per_patient), "\n")

# If assumptions are true, remove redundant columns
if (identical_ids) {
  data <- subset(data, select = -`Sample ID`)
}


if (length(unique_cancer_types) == 1) {
  data <- subset(data, select = -`Cancer Type`)
}

if (length(unique_study_ids) == 1) {
  data <- subset(data, select = -`Study ID`)
}

if (length(unique_sample_types) == 1) {
  data <- subset(data, select = -`Sample Type`)
}

if (length(unique_numbers_of_samples_per_patient) == 1) {
  data <- subset(data, select = -`Number of Samples Per Patient`)
}
#supressing id variables
data <- subset(data, select = -`Patient ID`)

# suppressing the sex variable
data <- subset(data, select = -`Sex`)

# suppressing the ER status
data <- subset(data, select = -`ER Status`)

# Due to the correlation, I think it is fair to remove Neoplasm Histologic Grade and mutation count, because they are respectivly highly correlated to notthingham prognostic index and TMB.
data <- subset(data, select = -`Neoplasm Histologic Grade`)
data <- subset(data, select = -`Mutation Count`)
data <- subset(data, select = -`Cohort`)

# because of NA issue in the cox model, these variable will be removed
data <- subset(data, select = -`Oncotree Code`)
data <- subset(data, select = -`Tumor Other Histologic Subtype`)

df <- data
# Confirm structure after cleaning
cat("\nColumns remaining after cleaning:\n")
print(names(data))
```

### HANDLING MISSING VALUES

```{r}
# Check missing data pattern
cat("Missing data summary:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(data)))
cat("\n")

# Prepare data for imputation
# Convert character variables to factors for mice
char_cols <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.character)]
for(col in char_cols) {
  data[[col]] <- as.factor(data[[col]])
}
```

```{r}
cat("Starting multiple imputation with mice...\n")
# Perform imputation (m=5 imputations, maxit=5 iterations)
imp <- mice(data, m = 5, maxit = 5, method = 'pmm', seed = 123, printFlag = FALSE)

cat("Imputation completed.\n")
# Use the first imputed dataset (you could also pool results across all m)
data_imputed <- complete(imp, 1)

# Verify no missing values
cat("\nMissing values after imputation:\n")
print(sum(is.na(data_imputed)))
```


### CHOOSE OUTCOME AND PREPARE SURVIVAL VARIABLES

```{r}
# Option 1: Relapse Free Status (RFS)
# Option 2: Overall Survival (OS)

# Let's prepare both and you can choose which to use
# For RFS:
data_imputed$rfs_time <- data_imputed$`Relapse Free Status (Months)`
data_imputed$rfs_event <- ifelse(data_imputed$`Relapse Free Status` == "1:Recurred", 1, 0)

# For OS:
data_imputed$os_time <- data_imputed$`Overall Survival (Months)`
data_imputed$os_event <- ifelse(data_imputed$`Overall Survival Status` == "1:DECEASED", 1, 0)

# CHOOSE YOUR OUTCOME HERE:
# Set outcome = "rfs" for Relapse Free Status or "os" for Overall Survival
outcome <- "rfs"  # Change this to "os" for Overall Survival

if(outcome == "rfs") {
  data_imputed$time <- data_imputed$rfs_time
  data_imputed$event <- data_imputed$rfs_event
  cat("\nUsing Relapse Free Status as outcome\n")
} else {
  data_imputed$time <- data_imputed$os_time
  data_imputed$event <- data_imputed$os_event
  cat("\nUsing Overall Survival as outcome\n")
}

# Check event distribution
cat("\nEvent distribution:\n")
print(table(data_imputed$event))
cat("Event rate:", mean(data_imputed$event), "\n")
```

### TRAIN-TEST SPLIT WITH STRATIFICATION

```{r}
set.seed(123)
# Stratified split based on event status
train_index <- createDataPartition(data_imputed$event, p = 0.75, list = FALSE)

train_data <- data_imputed[train_index, ]
test_data <- data_imputed[-train_index, ]

# Verify stratification
cat("\nTrain-Test Split Verification:\n")
cat("Train size:", nrow(train_data), "\n")
cat("Test size:", nrow(test_data), "\n")
cat("Train event rate:", mean(train_data$event), "\n")
cat("Test event rate:", mean(test_data$event), "\n")
```
### MODEL 1: STANDARD COX MODEL (LINEAR EFFECTS ONLY)

```{r}
# Select relevant predictors
# Exclude outcome variables and redundant columns
exclude_cols <- c("Relapse Free Status (Months)", "Relapse Free Status",
                  "Overall Survival (Months)", "Overall Survival Status",
                  "Patient's Vital Status", "time", "event", 
                  "rfs_time", "rfs_event", "os_time", "os_event")

predictor_cols <- setdiff(names(train_data), exclude_cols)

# Create formula for Cox model
# Wrap variable names with spaces in backticks
predictor_cols_clean <- paste0("`", predictor_cols, "`")
formula_cox1 <- as.formula(paste("Surv(time, event) ~", 
                                  paste(predictor_cols_clean, collapse = " + ")))

# Fit standard Cox model - remove NA coefficients
cox_model1 <- coxph(formula_cox1, data = train_data, x = TRUE)

# Check for NA coefficients and refit without problematic variables if needed
if(any(is.na(coef(cox_model1)))) {
  cat("\nWarning: Some coefficients are NA. Removing problematic variables...\n")
  na_vars <- names(coef(cox_model1))[is.na(coef(cox_model1))]
  cat("Variables with NA coefficients:", na_vars, "\n")
  
  # Identify base variable names (remove factor level suffixes)
  na_base_vars <- unique(gsub("`.+", "`", na_vars))
  predictor_cols_filtered <- setdiff(predictor_cols, gsub("`", "", na_base_vars))
  
  # Refit model
  predictor_cols_clean <- paste0("`", predictor_cols_filtered, "`")
  formula_cox1 <- as.formula(paste("Surv(time, event) ~", 
                                    paste(predictor_cols_clean, collapse = " + ")))
  cox_model1 <- coxph(formula_cox1, data = train_data, x = TRUE)
  
  # Update predictor_cols for Model 2
  predictor_cols <- predictor_cols_filtered
}

cat("\nModel 1 Summary:\n")
print(summary(cox_model1))

# Model diagnostics
cat("\nConcordance index (C-index) on train data:", 
    summary(cox_model1)$concordance[1], "\n")

# Test set performance
# risk_score_test1 <- predict(cox_model1, newdata = test_data, type = "risk")
cox_test1 <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ risk_score_test1, data = test_data)
cat("C-index on test data:", summary(cox_test1)$concordance[1], "\n")
```


### MODEL 2: EXTENDED COX MODEL (NONLINEAR & COMPLEX RELATIONSHIPS)

```{r}
cat("\n=== MODEL 2: Extended Cox Model with P-splines ===\n")

# Identify continuous and categorical variables
continuous_vars <- c("Age at Diagnosis", "Lymph nodes examined positive",
                     "Nottingham prognostic index", "TMB (nonsynonymous)",
                     "Tumor Size")

# Only keep continuous variables that exist in the data
continuous_vars <- intersect(continuous_vars, names(train_data))

# Create formula with pspline for continuous variables
pspline_terms <- paste0("pspline(`", continuous_vars, "`)", collapse = " + ")
categorical_vars <- setdiff(predictor_cols, continuous_vars)
categorical_terms <- paste0("`", categorical_vars, "`", collapse = " + ")

formula_cox2 <- as.formula(paste("Surv(time, event) ~", 
                                  pspline_terms, "+", categorical_terms))

# Fit extended Cox model with psplines
cox_model2 <- coxph(formula_cox2, data = train_data, x = TRUE)

cat("\nModel 2 Summary:\n")
print(summary(cox_model2))

# Model diagnostics
cat("\nConcordance index (C-index) on train data:", 
    summary(cox_model2)$concordance[1], "\n")

# Test set performance
# risk_score_test2 <- predict(cox_model2, newdata = test_data, type = "risk")
cox_test2 <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ risk_score_test2, data = test_data)
cat("C-index on test data:", summary(cox_test2)$concordance[1], "\n")
```

### MODEL COMPARISON

```{r}
# Compare models using AIC and likelihood ratio test
cat("\nModel 1 AIC:", AIC(cox_model1), "\n")
cat("Model 2 AIC:", AIC(cox_model2), "\n")

# Likelihood ratio test
lr_test <- anova(cox_model1, cox_model2)
cat("\nLikelihood Ratio Test:\n")
print(lr_test)
```

### VIZUALISATION

```{r}
# Kaplan-Meier curve for the entire dataset
km_fit <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ 1, data = data_imputed)
plot(km_fit, xlab = "Time (Months)", ylab = "Survival Probability",
     main = "Kaplan-Meier Survival Curve")

# Risk groups based on Model 2
risk_groups <- cut(predict(cox_model2, type = "risk"), 
                   breaks = quantile(predict(cox_model2, type = "risk"), 
                                    probs = c(0, 0.33, 0.67, 1)),
                   labels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"),
                   include.lowest = TRUE)

train_data$risk_group <- risk_groups
km_fit_risk <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ risk_group, data = train_data)

# Plot survival curves by risk group
ggsurvplot(km_fit_risk, data = train_data,
           pval = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE,
           risk.table = TRUE,
           title = "Survival by Risk Group (Model 2)",
           xlab = "Time (Months)",
           ylab = "Survival Probability",
           legend.labs = c("Low Risk", "Medium Risk", "High Risk"))
```
### BRIER SCORE ANALYSIS

```{r}
# Calculate Brier scores using riskRegression
# Define time points for evaluation (avoid extreme values)
max_time_eval <- quantile(test_data$time, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)
time_points <- seq(1, max_time_eval, length.out = 40)

# Calculate Brier scores for both models on test data
tryCatch({
  brier_model1 <- Score(list("Model 1" = cox_model1, "Model 2" = cox_model2),
                        formula = Surv(time, event) ~ 1,
                        data = test_data,
                        times = time_points,
                        metrics = "brier",
                        summary = "ipa",
                        se.fit = FALSE)
  
  cat("\nBrier Score Summary:\n")
  print(brier_model1)
  
  # Plot Brier scores as a function of time
  plotBrier <- plotBrier(brier_model1, 
                         main = "Brier Score over Time",
                         xlab = "Time (Months)",
                         ylab = "Brier Score")
  print(plotBrier)
}, error = function(e) {
  cat("\nError in riskRegression Score calculation:", e$message, "\n")
  cat("Continuing with custom IBS calculation...\n")
})
```

### INTEGRATED BRIER SCORE FUNCTION

```{r}
# Function to calculate Integrated Brier Score (IBS)
# Based on: https://square.github.io/pysurvival/metrics/brier_score.html
calculate_ibs <- function(model, newdata, time_col = "time", event_col = "event", 
                         max_time = NULL) {
  
  # Extract time and event from newdata
  time_obs <- newdata[[time_col]]
  event_obs <- newdata[[event_col]]
  
  # Set max_time if not provided
  if(is.null(max_time)) {
    max_time <- max(time_obs, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Create time grid for integration
  time_grid <- seq(0, max_time, length.out = 100)
  
  # Get survival predictions for each time point
  surv_pred <- predictSurvProb(model, newdata = newdata, times = time_grid)
  
  # Calculate Brier score at each time point
  brier_scores <- numeric(length(time_grid))
  
  for(i in 1:length(time_grid)) {
    t <- time_grid[i]
    
    # Predicted survival probability at time t
    S_pred <- surv_pred[, i]
    
    # Observed status at time t
    # Y(t) = 1 if event occurred before or at t, 0 otherwise
    Y_t <- ifelse(time_obs <= t & event_obs == 1, 1, 0)
    
    # For censored observations before t, we need to weight appropriately
    # Using Inverse Probability of Censoring Weighting (IPCW)
    
    # Fit censoring distribution (reverse Kaplan-Meier)
    cens_km <- survfit(Surv(time_obs, 1 - event_obs) ~ 1)
    
    # Get censoring weights at time t
    weights <- numeric(length(time_obs))
    for(j in 1:length(time_obs)) {
      if(time_obs[j] > t) {
        # Subject still at risk at time t
        weights[j] <- 1 / summary(cens_km, times = t)$surv
      } else if(event_obs[j] == 1) {
        # Event occurred before or at t
        weights[j] <- 1 / summary(cens_km, times = time_obs[j])$surv
      } else {
        # Censored before t
        weights[j] <- 0
      }
    }
    
    # Calculate weighted Brier score
    brier_scores[i] <- mean(weights * (Y_t - S_pred)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Integrate using trapezoidal rule
  ibs <- sum(diff(time_grid) * (brier_scores[-1] + brier_scores[-length(brier_scores)])) / 2 / max_time
  
  return(list(
    ibs = ibs,
    time_grid = time_grid,
    brier_scores = brier_scores
  ))
}

# Calculate IBS for both models on test data
cat("\nCalculating Integrated Brier Score on test data...\n")

ibs_model1 <- calculate_ibs(cox_model1, test_data)
ibs_model2 <- calculate_ibs(cox_model2, test_data)

cat("\nIntegrated Brier Score (IBS):\n")
cat("Model 1 (Linear):", round(ibs_model1$ibs, 4), "\n")
cat("Model 2 (P-splines):", round(ibs_model2$ibs, 4), "\n")

# Plot comparison of Brier scores over time
plot_data <- data.frame(
  Time = c(ibs_model1$time_grid, ibs_model2$time_grid),
  Brier_Score = c(ibs_model1$brier_scores, ibs_model2$brier_scores),
  Model = rep(c("Model 1 (Linear)", "Model 2 (P-splines)"), 
              each = length(ibs_model1$time_grid))
)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Time, y = Brier_Score, color = Model)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Brier Score over Time - Test Set",
       x = "Time (Months)",
       y = "Brier Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

#create profile
profiles <- data.frame(

  # Factors — ALL factor levels taken from your dataset
  `Type of Breast Surgery` = factor(
    c("BREAST CONSERVING", "BREAST CONSERVING", "MASTECTOMY"),
    levels = levels(train_data$`Type of Breast Surgery`)
  ),

  `Cancer Type Detailed` = factor(
    c("Breast Invasive Ductal Carcinoma",

    c("High", "Moderate", "Low"),

    c("NO", "YES", "YES"),
    levels = levels(train_data$`Chemotherapy`)
  ),

  `Pam50 + Claudin-low subtype` = factor(
    c("LumA", "Basal", "LumB"),
    levels = levels(train_data$`Pam50 + Claudin-low subtype`)
  ),

  `ER status measured by IHC` = factor(
    c("Positve", "Positve", "Negative"),
    levels = levels(train_data$`ER status measured by IHC`)

    c("Negative", "Negative", "Positive"),

  ),

    c("YES", "NO", "YES"),

  ),

### RANDOM FOREST (failed...)

```{r}


train_data_clean <- paste0("`", train_data, "`")
formula_cox1 <- as.formula(
  paste("Surv(time, event) ~", paste(predictor_cols_clean, collapse = " + "))
)

cox_model1 <- coxph(formula_cox1, data = train_data, x = TRUE)

valid_predictors <- predictor_cols_clean[predictor_cols_clean %in% names(train_data_clean)]

train_data_rsf <- train_data[, c("time", "event", valid_predictors)]

formula_rsf <- as.formula(
  paste("Surv(time, event) ~", paste(predictor_cols_clean, collapse = " + "))
)

rsf_default <- rfsrc(
  formula = formula_rsf,
  data = train_data,
  ntree = 1000,
  importance = TRUE
)


tune_result <- tune(
  formula_rsf,
  data = train_data,
  ntreeTry = 500,
  mtryStart = 2,
  nodesizeTry = c(5, 10, 20),
  stepFactor = 1.5,
  trace = TRUE
)

best_mtry     <- tune_result$optimal["mtry"]
best_nodesize <- tune_result$optimal["nodesize"]

rsf_tuned <- rfsrc(
  formula = formula_rsf,
  data = train_data,
  ntree = 1500,
  mtry = best_mtry,
  nodesize = best_nodesize,
  splitrule = "logrank",
  importance = TRUE
)


times_eval <- seq(12, 144, by = 12)  

bs_compare <- Score(
  list(
    Cox = cox_model1,
    RSF.default = rsf_default,
    RSF.tuned   = rsf_tuned
  ),
  formula = Surv(time, event) ~ 1,
  data = test_data,
  times = times_eval,
  metrics = c("Brier")
)

print(cox_model1)
print(rsf_default)
print(rsf_tuned)
print(tune_result)

plot(bs_compare, models = c("Cox", "RSF.default", "RSF.tuned"),
     main = "Brier Score Comparison: Cox vs RSF Models")

```
